deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page (Litt. S) holds Gauss's Ceres tables. They give mean longitudes for 1801–1811, a daily motion of 770.935", an eccentricity of 0.0785, a node near 80°53' and an inclination near 10°37'. They also contain reductions for the five oppositions I–V (1801–1805). This page (Litt. T) continues that work in two parts: (A) a small adjustment of inclination and node, and (B) an ephemeris of Ceres for its 1808 opposition.

(A) TOP BLOCK, first column: five equations of condition.
- The unknowns are i (correction to the inclination, in arc-seconds) and Ω (correction to the node, in arc-seconds).
- Each equation has the form v_k = n_k + a_k·i + b_k·Ω.
- By context these are most likely the latitude residuals of the five oppositions 1801–1805, since the same numbers appear in the margin of the previous page. This identification is my inference.
- The rows are:
  - v1 = +1.71 + 0.996 i + 0.0173 Ω
  - v2 = −9.57 − 0.329 i − 0.1730 Ω
  - v3 = −3.70 − 0.975 i + 0.0420 Ω (the sign of 0.975 is blotted; it must be minus, see checks)
  - v4 = +0.39 + 0.388 i − 0.1729 Ω
  - v5 = −11.16 + 0.638 i + 0.1446 Ω

TOP BLOCK, middle column: four further linear equations of normal-equation type.
- +1.29 + 2.635 i + 0.0717 Ω
- −0.50 + 0.307 i + 0.4738 Ω
- −0.64 + 0.014 i + 0.4658 Ω
- +1.36 + 2.591 i + 0.0040 Ω
- Rows 1 and 4 are essentially 'i-equations'. Their coefficients 2.635 and 2.591 are close to [aa] = 2.608 of the first block. Rows 2 and 3 are 'Ω-equations'.
- These are evidently the eliminating equations actually solved. Gauss's result is i = −0.53", Ω = +1.37".
- Each pair (1,2) and (3,4) taken separately gives i ≈ −0.53, Ω ≈ +1.39 to +1.40.
- All four rows vanish to within about 0.01" at (−0.53, +1.37).

TOP BLOCK, right column: the final residuals. Substituting i and Ω into the first block gives +1.20, −9.62, −3.13, −0.05, −11.31. My recomputation gives +1.21, −9.63, −3.13, −0.05, −11.30.

Assessment of block (A). This is a two-parameter correction of i and Ω from five oppositions, a standard step in Gauss's successive improvement of the Ceres elements. The exact provenance of the middle equations (which weights or which data) cannot be reconstructed from this page alone. Plain ordinary least squares on the five printed rows gives i ≈ −0.62, Ω ≈ +2.27, not Gauss's values. So he did not simply form unweighted normal equations from these five rows as printed. They may have been weighted, or combined with other data.

(B) EPHEMERIS: 'Ceres Örter 1808 für Pariser M[itter]N[acht] nach achten elliptischen Elementen'. The span is 1808 July 21 – August 18, daily, for Paris midnight. The columns are as follows; columns 1–4 were identified by my own rough reconstruction of Ceres' position.

Column 1: apparent right ascension in degrees, decreasing from 322°55'37" to 316°55'7" (retrograde).
- My check: with the previous page's elements, Ceres' heliocentric longitude around Aug 6–10 is ≈314.6°. Its geocentric latitude is ≈ −12.6°. This gives α ≈ 320° and δ ≈ −28.8°, matching the table.
- So column 1 is right ascension, not longitude.
- Struck-out values every four days differ from the adopted ones by 28'41" to 32'9" (a varying amount). They are a discarded earlier computation.

Column 2: daily change of right ascension in seconds of arc. It equals the mean of the adjacent first differences.
- Example: the Jul 21→22 difference is 11'9.64" = 669.64", and (661.96 + 676.95)/2 = 669.46.
- Example: the Aug 9→10 difference is 809.96", and (810.00 + 809.48)/2 = 809.74.
- The maximum retrograde rate, 810.00", falls on Aug 9.

Column 3: south declination, 27°24'35.5" increasing to 30°3'31.6".

Column 4: daily change of declination in seconds.
- Jul 21→22 difference 415.40 versus mean 415.30.
- Aug 17→18 difference 230.50 versus mean 230.57.

Column 5: a quantity symmetric about Aug 3–4, minimum 965.0. Most probably the aberration (light) time in seconds, i.e. ≈493 s × Δ, giving Δ_min ≈ 1.96 AU, consistent with Ceres near aphelion at opposition. This identification is mine and is not certain.

The table is internally very smooth. The second differences of RA run 14.6, 13.8, 13.1, 12.3, 11.5, 10.7, … .
errors: The first-block row 3 is printed in the transcription as +0.975i. Only −0.975i reproduces Gauss's own residual −3.13 (with +0.975i one gets −4.16). The blotted sign is a minus.
Last column, Jul 28: the transcription's 968.8 breaks the smooth sequence 968.7 → ? → 967.0. The value should be 967.8, which is overwritten in the manuscript; it is not an error by Gauss.

Ω = +1.37 is slightly smaller than the value (≈1.39–1.40) implied by solving either pair of middle equations exactly. The effect on the residuals is below 0.02", so this is only a rounding-level discrepancy.

Ordinary unweighted least squares on the five first-block rows as printed gives i ≈ −0.62", Ω ≈ +2.27", not Gauss's −0.53", +1.37". So the middle equations are not the plain normal equations of these rows; the procedure is not fully reconstructible from this page. This is not necessarily an error.
Struck-out RA values (every 4th day) are off by about 29'–32' and were rightly cancelled and replaced.

results.what: Correction of inclination and node of Ceres from five opposition residuals: i = −0.53", Ω = +1.37", with final residuals +1.20, −9.62, −3.13, −0.05, −11.31
results.modern_name: Differential correction of orbital elements by (least-squares-type) adjustment of equations of condition

results.what: Daily ephemeris of Ceres (RA, daily RA motion, south declination, daily declination motion, light time / distance-related quantity) for 1808 Jul 21–Aug 18, Paris midnight, from the 'eighth' elliptic elements
results.modern_name: Opposition ephemeris computed from Keplerian elements
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Ceres ephemerides published in Zach's Monatliche Correspondenz)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine computational astronomy, well documented as Gauss's: improvement of Ceres' node and inclination, then a daily opposition ephemeris for 1808. The only minor interest is the working detail of the adjustment.

checkable.asserts: Residual 1 after substituting i=-0.53, Om=1.37 is +1.20
Residual 3 equals -3.13 only if the i-coefficient is -0.975 (sign correction)
All four middle-column equations are satisfied by i=-0.53, Om=1.37 to within 0.02 arcsec
Pair (1,2) of middle equations gives i≈-0.528, W≈1.398
Column 2 is the daily RA motion: the Jul 21→22 RA difference (669.64") is the mean of the tabulated rates
Column 4 is the daily declination motion (Jul 21→22)
Ceres near opposition (lambda≈313.7°, beta≈-12.6°) has declination ≈ -28.8°, confirming column 3 is south declination

transcription_corrections: Row 3 of first block: '−3,70 − 0,975i + 0,0420Ω' (blotted sign is minus, not plus).
Jul 28, last column: probably '967,8' (overwritten), not '968,8'; the sequence requires 967.8.
Heading reads 'Ceres Örter 1808 für Pariser M. N. nach achten elliptischen Elementen' (M. N. = Mitternacht); the bracketed '[?]' after 'achten' can likely be removed.
Column 1 is right ascension in degrees (not longitude); struck-out entries are discarded earlier RA values.
